title: Choose the visual world for the N/01 film site
question: The roll assigned Depot Wayfinding: the page becomes the depot the car was filmed in. Keep it, take the alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Depot Wayfinding
options.lineage: Tram depot signage: stencilled bay numbers, hazard-striped columns, painted floor lanes (all in the footage)
options.thesis: The page is the depot: you drive down a painted lane and every chapter is a numbered bay.
options.viewport: The film full-bleed; a painted yellow lane line runs down the page edge as the timeline, a hazard-striped column carries a huge stencilled bay number, copy sits on a flat bolted sign plate.
options.risk: Tips into an industrial costume if the stencil and stripes are used everywhere instead of only where a depot would paint them.

raised.raise: The lane line is the one unbroken line on the page: it never wraps, and its marker always shows where the car is now.
Amber is reserved for the single commit action; safety yellow does wayfinding only.
The footer is a dense credit block built from the film's real metadata.
Every still carries an origin ticket: bay number and timecode.
Depth comes from flat overlapping plates only, never drop shadows.
Two spot inks, never more: stencil yellow and thread amber.

options.label: Tape Drawing Studio
options.lineage: 1:1 automotive tape drawings on vellum walls in design studios
options.thesis: The car is drawn in tape before it is built; the light thread is the one tape line that glows.
options.viewport: A pale vellum wall with the film pinned like a print, a single tape line sweeping from the hero into the next section.
options.risk: A light page fights the dark footage, and the tape-drawing look is familiar from car-design portfolios.

options.label: Drum Machine Step Row
options.thesis: The film's six chapters as sixteen step keys under a chase light.
options.viewport: The step row as the film's timeline, the chase light as the playhead.
options.case: Fuses with the scroll sound, but car-site visitors do not identify with a drum machine, and it blurs what is being sold.
options.kept: The one unbroken line that always tells you where now is.

options.label: Creator Hardware Bench
options.lineage: desk instruments with keycaps and knurled knobs
options.thesis: Scrub the film with a knurled knob; one orange key commits.
options.viewport: A gunmetal panel framing the film with a scrub knob and an amber readout.
options.case: Close to car instrumentation, but it frames the film as a gadget and loses to the depot on audience fit and clarity.
options.kept: Exactly one action colour, reserved for the action that matters.

options.label: Exploitation Combo Sheet
options.thesis: The car billed like a grindhouse double feature.
options.viewport: Two shouting titles over clipped stills.
options.case: Cheapens a luxury concept; loses on both axes.
options.kept: A dense billing block anchoring the foot.

options.label: Moon-Shadow Bazaar
options.thesis: Shadows traded by length and memory.
options.case: No link to the car; loses on both axes.
options.kept: Every item carries a ticket of origin.

options.label: Łowicz Papercut
options.thesis: Depth from pasted layers, no shading.
options.case: Folk craft against film footage; loses on both axes.
options.kept: Depth by overlap only, never by shading.

options.label: Risograph System
options.thesis: Two fluorescent inks misregistered on paper.
options.case: Zine culture, not car culture; loses on both axes.
options.risk: Wrong register for a luxury car.
options.kept: Strict limit of two spot inks.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The scroll-video car launch page, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Film full-bleed, chapter text over a dark gradient, specs and a reserve button.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other car launch site, which is what you just rejected.
